newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money tumbles on heavy allocation.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money tumbles on heavy allocation.

text.p: Dutch call money rates started to tumble early on Monday after the Dutch central bank allocated a hefty 8.39 billion guilders to the money market under a one-day special advances pact.

Dealers said they were surprised by the huge amount of liquidity flowing into the market after the allocation and some said they expected overnight money rates to dip as low as 2.00 percent, bringing it level with the secured loans rate.
Call money was bid at around 2.68 percent at the opening but slipped to 2.50 percent just after the allocation and at 0845 GMT trades were settled at around 2.38 percent bid.
Other money market rates were stable, with three-month deposits trading at 2.76 percent bid, unchanged from Friday.
The guilder was glued to Friday's central bank advisory rate of 112.18 per 100 marks.
Dealers said they expected the new special advances pact at 1400 GMT to be set at an unchanged 2.50 percent.
